# CodeSparring
# https://codesparring.dev

> CodeSparring is two things: a free, public curriculum that teaches Python, SQL, and system design
> the way interviews actually ask about them, and an AI mock-interview room where you practice
> talking through a problem out loud under time pressure. The reading half of every lesson is free
> and open to anyone, no account required.

Last reviewed: 2026-08-02. Every claim below was checked against the running code on that date.
The curriculum grows continuously, so this file deliberately describes tracks and levels rather than
lesson counts, which would be stale within a week.

## What CodeSparring is for

Most practice tools test whether you can solve a problem alone and in silence. An interview tests
something else: whether you can explain your reasoning while you work, recover when the interviewer
pushes back, and say why you chose one design over another. CodeSparring is built around that second
skill, and the Learn curriculum exists to give you something specific to say.

## Learn: the free public curriculum

Every lesson has three phases. The first is free and public. The second and third require an account.

1. **Read** (public, no account). The teaching body: prose, worked examples, diagrams, runnable demo
   code, and inline check questions that reveal their answer on click.
2. **Apply** (account required). A guided exercise with hints and a reference solution.
3. **Practice** (account required). The same idea without the scaffolding, graded by hidden tests.

Public lesson pages are static and indexable. The graded workspace is a separate URL, requires
sign-in, and is marked `noindex`.

### URL shape

- `/learn` is the hub.
- `/learn/{track}` is a track landing page. Tracks are `python`, `sql`, and `system-design`.
- `/learn/{track}/{levelSlug}` is a level index.
- `/learn/{track}/{levelSlug}/{lessonId}` is the canonical public lesson page. This is the URL to
  cite and the URL that appears in the sitemap.
- `/learn/{track}/{levelSlug}/{lessonId}/workspace` is the interactive graded player. It is
  auth-gated, never listed in the sitemap, and never indexed.

### Track: Python (`/learn/python`, 5 levels)

Aimed at someone who will be asked to write and defend Python in an interview, not at someone
learning to program for the first time. It concentrates on the behaviour that trips candidates up.

- **Level 1: Foundations** (`/learn/python/fundamentals`). Variables, types, loops, functions, and
  the traps inside them: float equality, integer division, truthiness, booleans as integers.
- **Level 2: Idioms** (`/learn/python/intermediate`). Comprehensions, generators, classes,
  dataclasses, decorators, and the standard-library idioms for dates, text, files, and APIs.
- **Level 3: Patterns** (`/learn/python/applied`). Modules, imports, typing, pathlib, sqlite3 with
  bound parameters, CLIs, packaging, and working across real files.
- **Level 4: Engineering** (`/learn/python/engineering`). Advanced OOP, descriptors, the GIL,
  threads versus processes, asyncio, profiling, and packaging.
- **Level 5: Judging Code You Did Not Write** (`/learn/python/verification`). Reading unfamiliar
  code, property-based testing, shrinking a failure, and reviewing AI-generated code that looks
  right and is not.

### Track: SQL (`/learn/sql`, 6 levels)

Written for data-engineering and analytics interviews. Exercises run against a real SQLite engine in
the browser and are graded on the result set they return.

- **Level 1: SQL Foundations** (`/learn/sql/foundations`). SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, types, NULL
  semantics, dates.
- **Level 2: Aggregation and Joins** (`/learn/sql/aggregation`). Aggregates, GROUP BY and HAVING,
  every join flavour, subqueries, CTEs.
- **Level 3: Data Modeling and Schema Design** (`/learn/sql/modeling`). DDL, keys, constraints,
  cardinality, normalization.
- **Level 4: Data Engineering with SQL** (`/learn/sql/engineering`). Window functions, recursive
  CTEs, slowly changing dimensions, idempotent merges, data-quality checks.
- **Level 5: Advanced and Company-Specific SQL** (`/learn/sql/advanced-company-sql`). The four
  rounds of a data-engineering loop rehearsed as graded SQL: power screen, modeling, pipeline, and
  system-design reasoning. Includes sessionization, join fan-out and skew, CDC changelog apply, and
  write-audit-publish quality gates.
- **Level 6: Cloud and Data Engineering Foundations** (`/learn/sql/cloud-data-foundations`). The
  platform underneath the query: object storage, columnar files and row groups, partitioning and
  pruning, bucketing, distributed execution, skew, orchestration. Taught as graded queries against
  simulated platform metadata. Beginner friendly; it can be started right after Level 2.

### Track: System Design (`/learn/system-design`, 12 levels)

The largest track. Lessons are free-response: read the material, write your own answer, then compare
it against a model answer. Level 0 through Level 11:

- **Level 0: Interview and Communication Method** (`/learn/system-design/interview-method`). Scoping
  a vague prompt, estimation, structuring the walkthrough, driving tradeoffs, level calibration.
- **Level 1: Foundations and Mental Models** (`/learn/system-design/foundations`). Networking, API
  contracts, real-time delivery options, idempotency, pagination, serialization, CDN basics.
- **Level 2: Data Storage and Modeling** (`/learn/system-design/data-storage`). Relational versus
  NoSQL, B-tree versus LSM, isolation levels, MVCC, access-pattern modeling.
- **Level 3: Scaling the Data Tier** (`/learn/system-design/scaling-data`). Replication, sharding
  and shard keys, caching and stampedes, search and vector indexes, CDC.
- **Level 4: Scaling Compute and Traffic** (`/learn/system-design/scaling-compute`). Load balancing,
  service discovery, gateways, rate limiting, load shedding, capacity planning, cell architecture.
- **Level 5: Distributed Systems Core** (`/learn/system-design/distributed-core`). CAP and PACELC,
  consistency models, clocks, consensus, two-phase commit, sagas, CRDTs, failure detection.
- **Level 6: Asynchronous and Event-Driven Systems** (`/learn/system-design/event-driven`). Queues,
  pub/sub and the log, Kafka internals, delivery semantics, stream processing, schema evolution.
- **Level 7: Reliability, Resilience and Operations** (`/learn/system-design/reliability-ops`). SLOs
  and error budgets, golden signals, OpenTelemetry, retries and circuit breakers, multi-region DR,
  progressive delivery, chaos engineering, postmortems.
- **Level 8: Security, Privacy and Multi-tenancy** (`/learn/system-design/security-privacy`).
  Passkeys, OAuth and OIDC, sessions and tokens, RBAC and ReBAC, encryption and secrets, abuse
  defense, compliance and DSAR.
- **Level 9: Modern Architecture and Delivery** (`/learn/system-design/modern-architecture`).
  Monolith versus microservices, DDD decomposition, Kubernetes, service mesh, serverless and edge,
  GitOps and IaC, FinOps, lakehouse and table formats.
- **Level 10: Applied Case Studies** (`/learn/system-design/case-studies`). Full-length "design X"
  interviews: URL shortener, rate limiter, typeahead, news feed, chat, ride sharing, file sync,
  video streaming, collaborative editor, key-value store, object store, message queue, distributed
  job scheduler, payment ledger, ad click aggregator, stock exchange, and more.
- **Level 11: Specialized and Frontier Systems**
  (`/learn/system-design/specialized-systems`). ML systems, feature stores, RAG architecture, vector
  databases and ANN, LLM inference serving, agents, evaluation and guardrails, real-time analytics,
  IoT and edge, time-series storage.

## Interview practice

- **AI interviewer.** A conversational interviewer that asks follow-ups, pushes on tradeoffs, and
  reacts to what you say rather than only to what you type.
- **Voice.** Speak your reasoning out loud, the way the real round works.
- **In-browser execution.** Monaco editor with Python running client-side via Pyodide and SQL via
  sql.js, so code runs without a server round trip.
- **Structured feedback.** Scored on communication, problem-solving approach, and code quality, not
  only on whether the tests pass.
- **Spaced repetition.** Reviews are scheduled for long-term retention. Two schedulers are in
  production at once, FSRS and SM-2, assigned per user as a live A/B, so the claim being tested is
  which one actually improves recall on this material.
- **Open learner model.** `/knowledge` shows the system's current belief about what you know, the
  evidence behind it, and a way to challenge or correct it.
- **Company-specific prep.** 38 companies with pattern-frequency data, including Google, Meta,
  Amazon, Apple, Netflix, Microsoft, Stripe, Airbnb, Uber, and Databricks.
- **Personalized roadmap.** A prep plan built from your target company, interview date, and measured
  skill gaps, blending DSA, bug-fix, and decomposition work.
- **Bug-fix and case labs.** Multi-file debugging scenarios and longer applied labs, not only
  single-function algorithm puzzles.

## Pricing

- **Free.** $0, no credit card. 8 full interview sessions per month, 20+ problems with unlimited
  practice, the AI interviewer with real-time feedback, performance tracking, and the whole Learn
  curriculum. No personalized roadmap, no spaced repetition scheduling, no pattern mastery tracking.
- **Pro.** $25/month, or $225/year, which works out to $19/month. 35 full interview sessions per
  month, unlimited re-practice within a scenario you have started, spaced repetition scheduling,
  personalized roadmap, pattern mastery tracking, company-specific prep, system-design interviews.
- **Enterprise.** Custom pricing for teams.

The Learn curriculum's reading half is free on every plan and requires no account at all.

## Who it is for

- Software engineers preparing for technical interviews at any level.
- Students and new grads applying for internships and first roles.
- Data engineering and analytics candidates, who are the SQL track's primary audience.
- Career changers who can solve problems but freeze when asked to narrate.

## Technology

- Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind, Firebase, deployed on Vercel.
- Interview conversation and feedback run on Gemini 3.6 Flash, with Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite for
  cheaper paths and DeepSeek as a fallback provider.
- Code execution is client-side: Pyodide for Python, sql.js for SQL. Nothing you run is sent to a
  server for execution.

## Crawling

- Sitemap: https://codesparring.dev/sitemap.xml
- robots.txt: https://codesparring.dev/robots.txt
- The canonical host is the apex, `https://codesparring.dev`. Requests to `www.codesparring.dev`
  are permanently redirected to it, so cite the apex.
- AI crawlers are explicitly welcome. GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, Claude-SearchBot, and
  Google-Extended are allowed everything a general crawler is allowed.
- Authenticated surfaces (`/practice`, `/sessions`, `/dashboard`, `/account`, `/admin`, `/api/`) are
  disallowed. They contain per-user state and nothing worth indexing.

## Founder

Built by Nikayel Ali Jamal, a computer science student at Sacramento State University, after
noticing that grinding problem sets did not transfer to the part of the interview where you have to
explain yourself.
